title: sigil.toml
description: Configuration for sigil, the autonomous evaluation and merge policy engine. See https://runsigil.com/reference/configuration/.

scenarios.description:
Where scenario source lives, as `[[scenarios]]` array-of-tables.

Defaults to a single `scenarios/` directory at the project root. Note
the plural: `[scenario]` (singular) is the unrelated reset-hook table
above, and [`validate_config`] rejects the confusable spellings.

health_timeout.description:
Maximum seconds spent polling `health_check` for HTTP 200 once the
environment is up — the **readiness** phase.

This is the only bound on readiness. Raising `startup_timeout` does not
give a slow-booting service more time to answer its health check.

startup_timeout.description:
Maximum seconds the backend's start command may run — the **startup**
phase. For the compose backend that is `compose up -d`: image pull plus
container create/start.

Honoured by the compose backend only; the other backends either return
immediately or do not deploy at all, and warn at config load when this
is set. Worst-case deploy time is `startup_timeout + health_timeout`.

teardown_timeout.description:
Maximum seconds the backend's teardown command may run — `compose down`,
`docker rm -f`, `kubectl delete namespace`.

Separate from `startup_timeout` because the two have opposite failure
preferences. Startup should fail fast: a wedged pull is not going to
improve. Teardown should try hard, because cutting it short leaks
containers and namespaces that nothing will come back for — so the
default is generous enough that a normal teardown never trips it, and
expiry is a last resort. When it does expire the child is killed and a
greppable warning names the environment, so an operator can reclaim
whatever was left behind (bn-1feq).

ComposeSubConfig.description: Configuration for the Docker Compose deploy backend (`[deploy.compose]`).

compose_template.description: Path to the compose template file (supports `${ARTIFACT_REF}`, `${PROJECT_NAME}`, `${PORT}`).

compose_command.description:
Shell command used to invoke compose-compatible tooling.
Defaults to `["docker", "compose"]`.

Examples:
- `['docker', 'compose']`
- `['podman', 'compose']`
- `['docker-compose']`

ContainerSubConfig.description: Configuration for the bare-container deploy backend (`[deploy.container]`).

image.description: Container image reference (overridden per-eval by the artifact ref).

port.description: Host port to expose the container on.

KubernetesSubConfig.description: Configuration for the Kubernetes deploy backend (`[deploy.kubernetes]`).

manifest_template.description: Path to the k8s manifest template.

kubeconfig.description: Optional path to a kubeconfig file (defaults to cluster in-context).

ProcessSubConfig.description: Configuration for the process deploy backend (`[deploy.process]`).

args.description: Arguments to pass to the command (e.g., `["run", "--bin", "my-api"]`).

env.description: Environment variables to set for the process.

working_dir.description: Working directory for the process (defaults to repo root).

port.description: Port the process will listen on. If omitted, assigned from hash like other backends.

stage_fail_rate_threshold.description:
Fraction of failing scenarios within a stage that triggers early
termination of the entire eval (BLOCK decision). Range: 0.0–1.0.

catastrophic_fail_rate.description:
Fraction of failing deterministic-tier scenarios above which the
semantic (LLM) stage is skipped entirely to save cost. Range: 0.0–1.0.

live_runners.description:
When `true` (default), `sigil.get/post/...` and `sigil.exec()` execute
real HTTP requests and subprocess commands.  When `false`, they return
stub responses.  Primarily used by tests; the real orchestrator keeps
the default (`true`).

allowed_origins.description:
Extra http(s) origins that origin-pinned first-party modes (`sigil
eval`, `sigil scenario run`, `sigil scenario generate`) may target
in addition to the deployed service's own origin, which is always
implicitly allowed (bn-irz0).  Use this for sidecar listeners the
scenarios legitimately hit via `opts.base_url` — e.g. `/metrics`
on `http://127.0.0.1:9090`.

Entries must be **bare** origins (`scheme://host[:port]`, optional
trailing `/`); default ports normalize (`http` → 80, `https` →
443).  Fail-closed: an entry that is not a valid bare http(s)
origin is a hard config error at load time, never a silently
skipped allowlist line.  One shared key covers all three modes —
the allowlist describes the deployment's sidecar topology, which
does not change per command.  `sigil run` (third-party contract
Lua) deliberately ignores it and stays pinned to its single
`--endpoint` origin (bn-3fne).

SECURITY: every origin listed here is a reachable exfiltration
target for scenario Lua, including HOLDOUT scenarios during
`sigil eval` — keep the list minimal and loopback-local.

denied_capabilities.description:
Scenario capabilities this project refuses to run (bn-37fi).

Every name must satisfy
[`crate::scenario::validate::is_known_capability`]; an unknown name is
a hard config error at load time, so a typo can never silently widen
what is allowed. Built-in names match ASCII
case-insensitively; `wasm.<name>` plugin identities use their exact
lowercase spelling, consistent with E005 and the runtime gate.

Empty (the default) denies nothing — sigil stays permissive unless
an operator opts in.

Enforced fail-closed at three layers:

1. **lint** — declaring a denied capability in `policy.capabilities`
   (or calling something that requires one) is lint error E007, so
   `sigil scenario lint` catches it in CI before anything runs;
2. **runtime** — `enforce_policy_runtime_capabilities` treats a
   denied capability as undeclared and installs the denying stub
   regardless of what the scenario declared;
3. **intent tools** — a denied capability is never exposed as a
   `sigil.intent` tool, even when the call asks for it by name.

SECURITY: `"exec"` is the motivating entry. `sigil.exec` runs
`sh -c <command>` on the **host running sigil** — not inside the
deployed container — so a CI that runs third-party or
agent-authored scenarios should deny it.

services.description:
Named services for cross-service scenarios (bn-3hbk): a
`name → base_url` map backing the `sigil.service("name")` Lua
handle. Declared as `services = { taxonomy = "http://twin-b:8080" }`
or an `[eval.services]` table.

Each value must be a **bare** http(s) origin
(`scheme://host[:port]`, optional trailing `/`), validated
fail-closed at load time with the same grammar as
[`Self::allowed_origins`]. Every declared service origin is *also*
implicitly added to the origin-pin set (like an `allowed_origins`
entry), so a scenario reaching a service via its handle stays
pinned while every other origin remains blocked. A `BTreeMap` keeps
iteration (and the "unknown service" error listing) deterministic.

SECURITY: like `allowed_origins`, every service origin is a
reachable target for scenario Lua — keep the map minimal.

path_patterns.description: File path to endpoint path patterns (e.g., "src/handlers/*.rs" -> "/api/*")

provider.description:
LLM provider: "ollama", "openai", "anthropic", "openrouter", "command".
Determines default api_base and API key env var.
When set to "command", LLM calls shell out to the `command` field instead
of using the HTTP API.

command.description:
Shell command for `provider = "command"`. The prompt is piped to stdin,
response read from stdout. Example: `"claude -p --output-format text"`

api_base.description: Optional API base URL override. If not set, derived from provider.

sast_mode.description: Mode for the SAST scanner. Defaults to advisory when a tool is configured.

secret_mode.description: Mode for the secret scanner. Defaults to advisory when a tool is configured.

dep_mode.description: Mode for the dependency scanner. Defaults to advisory when a tool is configured.

scanner_timeout_secs.description:
Per-scanner subprocess timeout in seconds. A scanner that runs longer than
this is killed and reported as a `Timeout` failure (fail-closed for
required scanners). Defaults to [`default_scanner_timeout_secs`].

ScannerMode.description:
Mode for a configured security scanner.

`Required` scanners must run successfully — a failure to execute or parse
their output is a hard gate failure (fail-closed). `Advisory` scanners stay
visible but their execution failures are non-blocking. `Disabled` scanners
are not run at all and never contribute to the gate.

OPAConfig.description:
OPA/Rego policy evaluator

Implements optional policy guardrails using Open Policy Agent (OPA).
Policies are defined in Rego language and evaluated against structured input
built from eval results, trust state, and security findings.

Disabled by default for backward compatibility.

enabled.description: Enable OPA policy evaluation (disabled by default)

policy_path.description: Path to OPA policy bundle directory or file

required.description: Require OPA to be installed; if false, silently skip on not found

timeout_seconds.description: Timeout for OPA evaluation in seconds

trusted_public_keys.description: Hex-encoded Ed25519 public keys trusted for verification.

GenerateConfig.description:
Configuration for `sigil scenario generate`.

LLM fields (provider, command, model, etc.) override `[judge]` settings
for generation. If a field is not set, falls back to `[judge]`.

context_specs.description: Spec files always included as context for every generation run.

system_prompt_extra.description:
Extra text appended to the scenario generation system prompt.
Use for domain-specific instructions (auth patterns, test data, naming).

contracts.description:
Optional schema contracts used to validate generated scenarios against
the service's declared request/response shapes. Absent = no contract
awareness (clean no-op). See [`GenerateContractsConfig`].

GenerateContractsConfig.description:
Configuration for `[generate.contracts]`.

Points scenario generation and candidate validation at machine-readable
API contracts. Currently only an OpenAPI 3.x JSON document is supported;
a future `json_schema_dir` key (a directory of standalone JSON Schema
files) is reserved but not yet implemented.

Paths are resolved relative to the project root, consistent with other
`[generate]` and `[deploy]` file paths.

openapi.description:
Path to an OpenAPI 3.x JSON document (e.g. `docs/openapi.json`).
When set, it is parsed into a contract index at pipeline start; a
missing, unreadable, malformed, or non-OpenAPI document is a hard
error (fail-closed), never a silently empty index.

ScenarioConfig.description:
Configuration for the `[scenario]` table.

Holds the `[scenario.reset]` hooks — HTTP requests the runner sends before
each scenario to reset in-memory state on the services under test
(rate-limit buckets, caches, etc.) so behaviour does not leak across
sequentially-run scenarios — and the `[scenario.env]` allowlist.

# Where reset hooks fire

- **`sigil scenario run`** (single scenario and `--all`): always. That
  path is sequential by construction.
- **`sigil eval`**: yes, since bn-n966 — once per scenario against *each*
  side, immediately before that side's body runs (the PR deploy, then the
  baseline deploy; named-service hooks resolve through the same
  `[eval] services` map for both, since declared services are external
  twins the two deploys share). A reset failure is that side's setup
  failure and that side alone: the body does not run, the other side is
  untouched, and the pair reads as a regression — fail-closed, never
  ALLOW.

  Because a hook resets state that **every** scenario in the set shares,
  eval refuses to run them in parallel: configured hooks together with
  `[eval] scenario_concurrency > 1` is an error raised before anything is
  deployed ([`crate::eval::execution::ensure_reset_hooks_can_fire`]). It
  is checked there, not at config load, so a `sigil.toml` with both a
  parallel `[eval]` and reset hooks stays usable under `sigil scenario
  run`.
- **`sigil run`**: yes since bn-qga0, but from flags rather than from this
  table — that mode reads no `sigil.toml` at all. `--reset
  [NAME=]METHOD:/path` (repeatable) and `--resets-from <PATH>` (a JSON
  array of objects with exactly this struct's fields) declare the same
  hooks, validated by the same [`validate_scenario_reset`] rules and fired
  by the same [`crate::runner::reset::run_reset_hooks`] helper before each
  scenario. `NAME` resolves against `--endpoint name=url` /
  `--endpoints-from` instead of `[eval] services`.

reset.description:
HTTP "reset hooks" sent before each scenario, in declaration order.

Two spellings, both parsing into this vector (bn-mzb7):

```toml
# one hook against the deploy's primary URL
[scenario.reset]
method = "POST"
path   = "/__sigil_test_reset"

# or several, each optionally naming an [eval] service
[[scenario.reset]]
method = "POST"
path   = "/__sigil_test_reset"

[[scenario.reset]]
method  = "POST"
path    = "/__sigil_test_reset"
service = "twin-b"
```

The first failing hook fails the scenario; later hooks are not sent.

env.description:
Environment variables exposed to scenarios through `sigil.env(KEY)`.

A **strict per-key allowlist**: only keys named here ever reach a
scenario, and `sigil.env` returns nil for everything else. This is the
eval-mode counterpart of `sigil run --env` (bn-3g11); before it existed
a scenario needing credentials during an eval had no supported way to
get them.

```toml
[scenario.env]
API_VERSION    = "v2"                            # literal
ALICE_PASSWORD = { from = "ALICE_PASSWORD" }     # passthrough
SERVICE_TOKEN  = { from = "CI_SERVICE_TOKEN" }   # renamed passthrough
```

Read from the **control snapshot**, like everything else the eval
consumes — a PR must not be able to widen its own allowlist.

ScenarioResetHooks.description:
JSON-schema shape of `[scenario.reset]`: one table, or an array of tables
(bn-mzb7).

Exists so `schemas/sigil-config.schema.json` describes both spellings.
Deserialization does NOT go through this enum — see
[`deserialize_reset_hooks`] for why — so it carries only `JsonSchema`.

anyOf.description:
`[scenario.reset]` — a single hook against the primary URL (or a
named service, if it sets `service`).
`[[scenario.reset]]` — several hooks, fired in declaration order.

ScenarioResetConfig.description:
HTTP request shape for one per-scenario reset hook.

Fields:
- `method`: HTTP method (e.g. `POST`, `DELETE`).
- `path`: path appended to this hook's target origin (e.g.
  `/__sigil_test_reset`). Absolute `http://...` URLs are not supported —
  a reset hook can only target the deploy under test or one of the
  `[eval] services` origins, so it can never leave the pinned origin set.
- `service`: optional `[eval] services` name to target instead of the
  deploy's primary URL (bn-mzb7). The same map `sigil.service("name")`
  reads; an undeclared name is a config error at load time. Unset means
  the primary URL.
- `headers`: optional request headers.
- `body`: optional request body (sent verbatim as a string).
- `expected_status`: expected response status. Any 2xx response is
  accepted when `expected_status` is unset.

Hooks fire under `sigil scenario run` and `sigil eval` (per scenario, per
side) — see [`ScenarioConfig`] for the exact semantics and why eval refuses
them under `scenario_concurrency > 1`. `sigil run` builds values of this
same struct from `--reset` / `--resets-from` (bn-qga0): `--resets-from`
deserializes straight into it, so the JSON field names are exactly the
ones documented above.

service.description:
Named `[eval] services` entry to reset; `None` targets the deploy's
primary URL (bn-mzb7).

anyOf.description:
A literal value written in the config. Fine for non-secrets; anything
sensitive belongs in [`Self::FromProcess`] so it stays off disk and out
of the control ref's history.

Read from sigil's own process environment at eval time, under the name
`from`. The value never touches the config, argv, or the ledger — the
same reason `sigil run --env KEY` has a bare form.

from.description: Name to read from sigil's process environment.

ScenarioDirConfig.description:
One root directory containing scenario source.

```toml
[[scenarios]]
path = "scenarios"                  # contains per-service subdirectories

[[scenarios]]
path = "services/api/scenarios"     # IS the api service's scenarios
service = "api"
```

One schema covers both shapes so a monorepo can colocate scenarios with the
service they exercise instead of forcing one central tree.

path.description:
Path to the directory, relative to the project root (the directory
containing `.sigil/`).

service.description:
When set, this directory *is* that service's scenarios and contains no
service-name level. When absent, the directory holds one subdirectory
per service.

Making the service explicit is what lets scenarios live anywhere: the
service used to be read positionally from the first path component,
which only works when every root shares one layout.

BrowserConfig.description:
Configuration for the `[browser]` table.

Future fields (per-scenario user-data-dir policy, version pinning) land
here as Phase 4+ wiring requires.

backend.description: Which backend the Lua `sigil.browser.*` methods dispatch through.

headless.description:
When `true`, Chrome launches with `--headless=new`; when `false` a
visible window is shown.  Defaults to `true`.

Override at run time via the `SIGIL_BROWSER_HEADLESS` env var —
`"0" | "false" | "no"` flip it to headful, anything else (including
unset) keeps the configured value.  See
[`BrowserConfig::resolve_headless`].

BrowserBackendKind.description:
Browser backend selector for `[browser] backend = "native" | "cli"`.

Default is `Native` (in-process Chrome-for-Testing runner from the
[`sigil-browser`](::sigil_browser) crate).

The `Cli` variant is retained **for config compatibility only**:
the legacy `agent-browser` shell-out path was removed in the Phase 6
final task (bn-1w5f). Setting `[browser] backend = "cli"` will
deserialize successfully but every `sigil.browser.*` call will
return a structured "removed" error pointing operators at the
native backend. See
[`crate::runner::browser::CLI_BACKEND_REMOVED_MESSAGE`].

The flag is read in [`crate::runtime::globals::install_browser`].

oneOf.description:
Removed CLI backend. Retained only so old `sigil.toml` files
continue to parse; selecting this value yields a structured
failure on every browser call.

require.description:
Project plugin requirements. String entries use the permanent official
`github:sigil-plugins/NAME` source; third-party sources must be named
explicitly in a deny-unknown inline table.

allow_third_party.description:
Permit explicit non-official GitHub sources and local authoring, in
addition to their required source and capability allowlists.

github.description:
GitHub API authentication settings. Tokens are read only by explicit
networked plugin-manager commands and never persisted. These settings
cannot add an official repository, workflow, issuer, or trust root.

trust.description:
Source and requested-capability policy for every live plugin boundary.
Allowlists can only narrow live authority; official provenance identity
and supported trust roots are closed, built-in Sigil policy.

grants.description: Operator-owned host capability grants, keyed by canonical plugin name.

runtime.description: Host-enforced limits for each scenario's plugin runtime.

anyOf.description: Explicit third-party source and SemVer range.

PluginGithubConfig.description: GitHub distribution settings for networked plugin-manager commands.

token_env.description:
Environment variable containing an optional GitHub token. The value is
deliberately not part of this configuration model.

PluginTrustConfig.description:
Source policy for installing and executing plugins.

This is not a publisher-key, OIDC-policy, or trust-root configuration
surface. Matching a source pattern never creates official provenance.

holdout_allowlist.description:
Canonical exact GitHub sources or owner-wide `github:owner/*` patterns
permitted to appear in holdout scenarios. This only narrows the
separately verified source identity.

install_allowlist.description:
Sources accepted for installation and all live plugin use. This only
narrows authority and cannot promote local, third-party, or legacy
digest-only bytes to official provenance.

capability_allowlist.description: Source policy independently applied to every requested capability.

PluginCapabilityAllowlistConfig.description: Source allowlists for each authority-bearing plugin capability.

PluginGrantConfig.description: Bounded authority granted to one plugin.

secrets.description: Named secret allowlist over the existing scenario environment source.

entropy.description: Permit nondeterministic OS bytes and mark replay best-effort.

log.description: Permit bounded guest log accounting; payload bytes are never emitted.

PluginNetworkGrant.description: Host-owned policy for one named outbound TCP endpoint.

target.description:
Logical service-map key and deploy port, for example `mysql:3306` or
`singlestore-pipelines.sql:3306`.

tls_server_name.description: Exact SNI and certificate verification name for TLS modes.

io_timeout.description: Synchronous read, write, flush, and TLS deadline.

max_connections.description: Concurrent open stream ceiling for this endpoint and lane.

max_bytes.description: Combined transferred-byte budget for this endpoint and lane.

oneOf.description: TLS before the guest receives the stream.
One host-owned TLS upgrade after protocol negotiation.

PluginSigV4Grant.description: Host-owned policy for one opaque SigV4 signed exchange.

endpoint.description: Existing logical endpoint in this plugin's network grant.

authority.description:
Signed HTTP `Host` authority. This never participates in routing and
need not equal the named service used to resolve the socket.

opaque_max_encoded_bytes.description:
Maximum encoded ASCII bytes for one optional opaque value. This rule
is available only to plugins on host API 1.2 or newer.

PluginRuntimeConfig.description:
Host-enforced plugin runtime limits.

These defaults are the single configuration source for the Wasmtime host,
the generated JSON Schema, the init template, and runtime evidence.

max_memory.description:
Aggregate WebAssembly linear-memory and currently live Sigil-owned host
allocation budget for one component instance, written as binary bytes
(`B`, `KiB`, `MiB`, or `GiB`). Host allocations include persistent
adapter objects and transient conversion buffers. The same value is
also the per-memory ceiling.

max_table_elements.description:
Aggregate element budget for all WebAssembly tables in one component
instance. The same value is also the per-table ceiling.

max_call_seconds.description: Wall-clock deadline for each outer Lua-visible call.

fuel.description: Guest fuel reset immediately before each outer Lua-visible call.

max_open_resources.description: Maximum live host-owned resource handles in one component instance.

max_component_instances_per_scenario.description: Maximum live component instances for one scenario and environment.

max_random_bytes_per_call.description: Maximum deterministic-random or entropy bytes returned by one call.

max_random_bytes_per_scenario.description:
Combined deterministic-random and entropy byte budget for one plugin,
scenario, and environment.
